label: Sho
note: Tibetan yoghurt, also churned for butter

about.text: Sho is the Tibetan word for the yoghurt made from the milk of the dri, the female yak. It is the usual first step of Tibetan butter-making and gives its name to the Shoton yoghurt festival.

links.name: Wikipedia, Yak butter; Oxford Companion to Food, Yak (via ckbk)

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Whole yak milk has nearly twice the fat of cow milk, so the set yoghurt is rich enough to be churned into butter.

processing.text: Yak milk, boiled and cooled, sets overnight or in several hours; the sources do not state the cultures.
